**Gap re-verified in current `main` code (still open, 2026-08-22):**

1. `cmd_terminate` (pod_lifecycle.py:4628) sets
   `target = _canonical_pod_name(args.issue, name_suffix) if name_suffix else None`.
   With no `--name-suffix`, `target is None` so `live_matches` stays the full
   `_live_pods_for_issue(issue)` set — every live pod resolving to the issue.
   There is no selector expressing "only the unsuffixed `pod-<N>`".
2. `_guard_keep_running_before_terminate` (pod_lifecycle.py:4094) short-circuits
   on `name_suffix is not None`, so the issue-wide `keep-running` tag blocks
   exactly the bare form and nothing else.

Both halves of the body's "The gap" section reproduce against HEAD. Nothing

**New finding the task body did not know about — a latent unsanctioned
primary-only selector already exists.** `terminate` does NOT validate
`--name-suffix` against `RUNPOD_NAME_SUFFIX_RE` (only `provision` does, at
pod_lifecycle.py:3135). So an empty-string suffix is accepted, and because
`_canonical_pod_name` branches on truthiness (`... if name_suffix else
f"pod-{issue}"`), an empty suffix resolves `target` to exactly `pod-<N>` —
while simultaneously tripping the `is not None` short-circuit that waives the
`keep-running` shield. The sketch's "`--name-suffix ""` given explicit
meaning" is therefore already de-facto reachable, as an accident, in the
weakest possible form: primary-only teardown with the issue-wide shield
silently waived and no confirmation that the operator meant the primary. That
is a hole to close in the same round as the feature, not a head start.

**Decision on the one delegated design question** (`keep-running` semantics —
the body says "Naming the intended semantics IS most of the task"; autonomous
session, so this is decided here and reviewed by the planner + critic
ensemble, per § Autonomous session behavior):

A primary-only form must NOT inherit the surgical path's blanket shield waiver.
Direction handed to the planner: the primary-only selector is an EXPLICIT,
validated flag that resolves exactly `pod-<N>`, and it stays SUBJECT to the
`keep-running` shield unless the shield's own per-pod evidence clears the
primary specifically — i.e. reuse the #1961 named-shield reasoning (a
structured `pod=<name>` / lead-position `epm:run-launched` note shielding a
NAMED pod) so a tag set solely to shield `pod-<N>-<slug>` does not block
`pod-<N>`, while a tag with no per-pod attribution keeps blocking everything
(fail toward not destroying). `--force-keep-running` remains the recorded-reason
override. Rationale: it closes the filed gap without opening a second door
around the shield (constraint 2 of the body), and it is the lower-risk of the
two options the body names — ignoring the tag outright defeats the tag.
Constraint 1 is non-negotiable and unchanged: the new form goes through
`_guard_upload_verification_before_terminate` (incl. the `outroot=` / `rows=`
attestation tokens) and `_guard_owner_fence_before_terminate` exactly as the
existing forms do.
